source.title: Feasibility of dopamine as a vector-valued feedback signal in the basal ganglia.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)

confidence_rationale: Directly implements the exact substrate ARC-108 proposes -- a local three-factor corticostriatal plasticity rule (presynaptic firing x postsynaptic factor x perceived dopamine concentration) with dopamine carrying a teaching signal -- and proves it increases the capacity to learn multidimensional real-valued outputs, which is precisely the 'learned gating weights on the E3 selector' function ARC-108 wants. High source quality (PNAS, formal proof + simulation). Mapping fidelity strong but not perfect: the paper's headline is a vector-valued (per-neuron) dopamine signal, whereas ARC-108's V3-minimal slice currently assumes a signed scalar RPE; the three-factor rule itself transfers cleanly, the vector-vs-scalar refinement is ARC-108's v4 routed-efferent territory.
failure_signatures: If REE keeps a single homogeneous scalar RPE broadcast to all gating weights, the paper's capacity result predicts a hard ceiling on how many independent channels the learned gating can resolve -- a scalar teaching signal cannot supply independent per-channel gradients.

The three-factor rule's power depends on a postsynaptic eligibility factor co-defining the update; a purely Hebbian-times-global-RPE rule without a credit-assigning postsynaptic term will misassign credit across simultaneously-active channels.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A local three-factor corticostriatal plasticity rule -- presynaptic firing rate x a postsynaptic factor x the unique dopamine concentration perceived by each striatal neuron -- lets dopamine act as a vector-valued error feedback signal (a loss gradient), increasing the capacity to learn a multidimensional series of real-valued outputs, and remains compatible with diffuse volume transmission rather than precise nigrostriatal wiring.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-108's core mechanism: replace the pure-arithmetic ARC-107 arbitration layer with cortico-striatal gating weights that are LEARNED by a three-factor rule (Hebbian channel co-activation x signed dopaminergic RPE). The paper supplies the formal feasibility and the capacity argument for exactly this teaching-signal-into-gating-weights substrate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's strongest result is for a vector-valued (per-neuron) dopamine signal; ARC-108's V3-minimal slice uses a signed scalar RPE. The three-factor learning rule maps directly, but the 'capacity to learn many independent outputs' result is partly a property of the vector signal, which is ARC-108's v4 routed-efferent refinement, not the v3 slice.
mapping.source_context: Computational/theoretical model of basal-ganglia learning; in-silico, no animal data.

confidence_components.notes: For an architectural-commitment claim, mapping_fidelity is weighted heaviest; the rule maps almost one-to-one, hence 0.82 aggregate despite the scalar-vs-vector caveat.
